articles.title: A multicenter, prospective, phase 2 trial on proton re-irradiation for patients with previously treated head and neck cancer
articles.summary: This phase 2 trial evaluates the outcomes of proton re-irradiation for head and neck cancer patients. Findings suggest promising locoregional control and survival, although late toxicity remains a key consideration in this patient population.

articles.title: AAPM Medical Physics Practice Guideline 18.a: Superficial radiation therapy using low-energy kilovoltage x-rays
articles.summary: This AAPM guideline provides updated standards for superficial radiation therapy (SRT) in dermatology and oncology. It outlines essential medical physics practices for system commissioning, quality assurance, and safe clinical delivery of low-energy x-rays.

articles.title: A Large Language Model Framework for Seed Implant Brachytherapy: Adaptive Weight Optimization via Retrieval-Augmented Generation
articles.summary: This study introduces an adaptive framework for brachytherapy treatment planning that utilizes large language models to automate and optimize objective function weights. The approach aims to reduce manual planning inefficiencies and enhance plan quality through iterative optimization.

articles.title: A multicenter end-to-end postal audit of skin markerless surface-guided radiation therapy
articles.summary: A multi-institutional audit evaluated the accuracy of markerless surface-guided radiation therapy (SGRT). While the technology achieved high static irradiation precision, researchers identified potential risks for setup errors that warrant careful workflow management.

articles.title: Retrospective analysis of machine service logs and EPID-based linac QA
articles.summary: This study demonstrates that integrating linear accelerator service logs with automated electronic portal imaging device (EPID) quality assurance data provides better insight into machine performance. The analysis highlights correlations between maintenance events and changes in beam characteristics.

articles.title: Analysis on radiation protection of FLASH treatment in conventional proton therapy facilities
articles.summary: This study evaluates the radiation safety of FLASH irradiation using the Varian ProBeam system. Results suggest that current conventional shielding is sufficient to maintain occupational and environmental safety for FLASH delivery.

articles.title: A cell-type resolved proton RBE model for potential clinical application
articles.summary: Researchers developed a new RBE model that accounts for cell-type specific repair capabilities. This model shows strong agreement with experimental data and aims to improve clinical accuracy in proton dose calculation.

articles.title: Differentiable Autoplanning Algorithm for Proton Therapy Based on Deep Learning
articles.summary: This study introduces a proof-of-concept framework for gradient-based optimization of proton therapy beam parameters. The approach utilizes a differentiable dose engine to potentially improve the automation of treatment planning.

articles.title: Angle-Dependent Dose Transformer Algorithm for Fast Proton Therapy Dose Calculations
articles.summary: The Angle-Dependent Dose Transformer Algorithm (ADoTA) is presented as a deep learning-based proton dose engine. It offers Monte Carlo-level accuracy while significantly speeding up calculation times for thoracic treatment plans.

articles.title: Experimental validation of time-driven proton PBS FLASH delivery on a clinical proton therapy system
articles.summary: This paper validates a method for time-driven proton pencil beam scanning at ultra-high dose rates. The findings provide a platform for preclinical FLASH research using existing clinical proton delivery infrastructure.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence in image-guided cervical interventional radiotherapy: a systematic review
articles.summary: This review examines the role of AI in automating workflow steps for cervical interventional radiotherapy. While showing high technical potential, the authors emphasize the need for robust external validation before routine clinical adoption.

articles.title: Radiation therapy quality assurance (RT QA) of adjuvant fractionated radiotherapy for WHO grade 2 atypical meningioma in the ROAM/EORTC1308 trial
articles.summary: This study underscores that pre-trial quality assurance is insufficient for complex radiotherapy of uncommon tumors, highlighting the need for prospective independent central reviews. Consistent high-quality radiotherapy across sites was achieved, ensuring the robustness of primary trial outcomes.

articles.title: 50 million Americans live in counties without a radiation oncology clinic, study finds
articles.summary: A recent study released by the American Society for Radiation Oncology (ASTRO) highlights significant geographic disparities in access, finding that 50 million Americans reside in counties that lack a radiation oncology clinic. This research underscores critical gaps in the distribution of radiation therapy infrastructure across the United States.

articles.title: ASTRO updates guideline on shorter-course radiation therapy for localized prostate cancer
articles.summary: The American Society for Radiation Oncology (ASTRO) has released updated clinical guidelines regarding the use of shorter-course radiation therapy for patients with localized prostate cancer. These updates aim to standardize hypofractionated treatment approaches based on current clinical evidence.

articles.title: IBA treats first patient in clinical trial of FLASH proton therapy for head and neck cancer
articles.summary: IBA has announced the treatment of the first patient in the C-FLASH-01 clinical trial, which aims to evaluate the safety and efficacy of ConformalFLASH proton therapy for head and neck cancer. This milestone represents a significant advancement in the development of ultra-high dose rate radiotherapy delivery.

articles.title: Hampton University Proton Cancer Institute opens new wellness space for patients and caregivers
articles.summary: The Hampton University Proton Cancer Institute has expanded its clinical facilities by opening a new wellness space dedicated to supporting patients and their caregivers during treatment. This development aims to enhance the patient experience at the regional proton therapy center.

articles.title: BayCare opens proton therapy center at Tampa's St. Joseph’s Hospital
articles.summary: BayCare Health System has opened a new $33 million proton therapy center at St. Joseph's Hospital in Tampa, expanding access to specialized radiation treatment in the region. The facility is equipped to provide precise proton beam delivery for various cancer indications.

articles.title: Medicare change could cost standalone proton therapy centers millions
articles.summary: A proposed Medicare pricing change threatens the financial stability of standalone proton therapy centers by significantly reducing reimbursement rates compared to hospital-based facilities. This change could impact research, patient support services, and future development of specialized proton therapy centers across the nation.
